lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with the basics: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. You can still qualify for Child Benefit for a child who is 16 or over, as long as they're under 20 and staying in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He actually left school recently, but he has signed up with the local careers service to help him figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail.

According to the rules, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks**.

**How long ago did Alex register with the careers service?** I need to know if it's been less than or more than 20 weeks since he registered.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been less than 20 weeks - only a few weeks ago actually. He just registered recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me also ask a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester, and Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (In other words, is anyone else - such as another parent or guardian - currently receiving Child Benefit for him?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

(This doesn't affect your eligibility, but it may mean you have to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit received.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I haven't really thought about the income side of things. I'm just trying to find out if I'm eligible to claim it in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - the income question doesn't affect whether you're eligible, it would only affect whether there's a tax charge to pay later. Since you're unsure, we can proceed with the eligibility assessment based on what you've told me.

Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

## Good News - You Are Eligible!

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Here's why:

Even though Alex is 17 and not currently in education or training, he recently registered with your local government-sponsored careers service. Under the Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for **up to 20 weeks** after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training if they register with a careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex registered only a few weeks ago, you're well within that 20-week period. You also meet the other key criteria:
- You live with Alex in the UK
- You're responsible for him
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

### What to do next:

You can apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already. Please note that this eligibility will last for up to 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. If during that time Alex starts approved education, training, or work (under 24 hours per week while in approved education/training), your eligibility may continue beyond the 20 weeks.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
